runner.note: scripts/repository/validate_planning_artifacts.py already executes the adapter-one identity-strip cases as a Python stage. That stage is a validator and not a runner: it emits no result document, declares no subject, and cannot report the divergence class the harness contract requires.

cases.title: Accept the agent registry and its recorded capability verdicts
cases.note: Every certification in the registry is empty or planned, so this case proves the registry is well formed and never that a tuple is exercised.

cases.title: Strip exactly the five Claude Code identity attributes inside the receiver
cases.note: D-099 makes removal a collector obligation performed at the device boundary rather than a configuration option, because no documented vendor setting removes user.email.

cases.title: Accept a well-formed observed datapoint from the adapter-one receive surface
Refuse a source observation carrying a raw user email
Refuse a source observation carrying an organization identifier
Refuse a source observation carrying a provider account identity
Refuse a normalized event that reintroduces an identity attribute after the receive stage
cases.note: The second stage is a separate case because a strip performed once and not enforced again is a strip that survives only until somebody adds a field.

cases.title: Two orderings of one compatibility tuple produce one digest
cases.note: The schema states the digest is over the RFC 8949 core deterministic encoding so two implementations cannot disagree about a tuple's identity. Nothing proved it. The two records hold identical values in opposite key order at every level; a reader preserving insertion order would give one certified tuple two identities, so a re-serialised tuple would miss its own certification.

cases.title: Changing any one component changes the tuple identity
cases.note: Atomic means atomic: observation mode, platform profile, source version floor, accounting arithmetic and privacy strip list each change the digest. A certification of one combination says nothing about any other, and this is the case that would fail if the digest covered only part of the record. A mutated tuple resolves to no certification, which is exactly what CLAIM_ADAPTER_UNSUPPORTED refuses; the tuple is looked up by digest under D-058, so a changed dimension is not a degraded certification but an absent one.
